subject: Post-demo: NeuroLex model-fit & safety action plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.p@neurolex.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: NeuroLex model-fit & safety action plan

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Per our call, I captured a concise recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run the first set of fit and safety checks.

Top takeaways from the discovery:
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant for pre-visit symptom intake (text only).
- Hard constraints: must refuse diagnostic advice for high-severity phrasing and escalate to human clinician.
- Latency target: 200ms p95 for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Cost target: unit economics should be within expected range for MVP (we discussed batching/caching options).

Model-fit recommendation (initial shortlist):
1) LlamaX-7B-q4f (fast, lowest latency; fine for structured intake with strong prompt engineering)
2) Optima-13B-pt (better out-of-the-box refusal behavior on sensitive medical prompts)
3) Redwood-Safety-13B (our curated variant with guardrail tokenizers and policy layers)

Planned evals we discussed:
- Functional: throughput & latency traces using your typical prompt distribution (we'll run real-sampled logs you share).
- Quality: clinical NLP metrics + human-rated accuracy on 120 prompt pairs (we suggest stratified by severity).
- Safety/refusal: targeted refusal/regression suite (sensitive-ask, jailbreak, explicit misinformation prompts).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Please share 50–100 anonymized example prompts (PII scrubbed) representing high/medium/low severity.
- Let us know who on your side should receive the SOC/compliance artifacts (if procurement wants them, include contact).

Deliverables we will send in 48–72 hours:
- A short benchmark report (latency & throughput) for the three candidates listed above. Link to the live eval: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/DL-3921-summary
- A curated prompt-set (attached as neurolex_mvp_prompt_set_v1.txt) for your review.
- Safety regression summary CSV (eval_runner_summary_QA.csv) after the first run.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You: share the prompt samples and confirm compliance contact by 2026-10-14 end of day.
- Us: run bench + safety suite and deliver summary by 2026-10-15 EOD.
- Follow-up call: Thurs 2026-10-15 11:00am PT to review grades and recommended model/rollout path.

If that looks right to you, I'll lock the follow-up and kick the evals with David.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: neurolex_mvp_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt examples), eval_runner_summary_QA.csv (blank template for results)
From: Maya Patel <maya.p@neurolex.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dr. Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@neurolex.com>, procurement@neurolex.com
Date: 2026-10-12T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NeuroLex model-fit & safety action plan

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt samples: we'll send 75 anonymized transcripts from our intake form (scrubbed) by EOD 2026-10-14. Those include ~12 high-severity flags (suicidal ideation, chest pain) that must be escalated.

2) Regulated data: some samples originate in our EU clinics. We need to confirm the model execution location (can Redwood guarantee EU-hosted inference for those records?) If not, we need to discuss either regional routing or a Private deployment.

3) Safety expectations: we need a documented failure mode for the model — what exact fallback does Redwood recommend when the model outputs diagnostic text? (We discussed hard refusals + human handoff; would like the concrete prompt templates you plan to use).

4) Procurement loop: procurement@neurolex.com should get SOC2 and IP/custody language.

We'll confirm the compliance contact and send the sample set. Looking forward to the eval results.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Product, Clinical ML | NeuroLex Health
maya.p@neurolex.com

Hi Maya — David from Solutions Eng here. Quick notes on the regional question and the safety fallback.

1) Region: for the first pass we can run the evals in our US-hosted sandbox (low latency, reproducible), but for production NeuroLex can choose EU-hosted inference via our Private or VPC options; routing per-request by customer-id is supported. I'll flag an ops note for the region-aware routing docs.

2) Concrete refusal strategy we propose (will provide templates):
- Detection layer: a policy classifier that tags whether an output contains "medical-diagnostic" content above a severity threshold.
- Prompt-level guardrails: use a system prompt that enforces refusal behavior and a structured JSON completion format when non-diagnostic content is allowed. Example: 
  "If the user asks for diagnosis or life-or-death decision, respond with: 'I am not able to provide medical advice. I will escalate this to your care team.' Then emit escalate=true in metadata."
- Escalation hook: the model returns a structured token the Redwood runtime uses to trigger an automatic human-notify workflow (we'll demo the webhook/Playbook).

3) Tests we will run in the safety suite: sensitive-ask probes, jailbreak variants, hallucination-focused QA pairs. Each probe will be tagged pass/fail and we'll provide concrete failure examples and recommended prompt refinements.

I'll upload the initial safety prompt templates and the small evaluation harness to the shared Drive link by EOD.

Regards,
David Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: redwood_safety_prompt_templates_v1.txt (will upload), region-routing-note.pdf (Ops note)
From: Maya Patel <maya.p@neurolex.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: NeuroLex model-fit & safety action plan

Thanks David — that allays a lot of our immediate concerns. A few final items before we hand the prompt set over: 

- Please include an explicit sample of the structured refusal JSON you mentioned so our engineers can wire the escalate=true flag into our triage system.
- On latency: can you surface p95 numbers for short prompts for each candidate model (LlamaX-7B-q4f, Optima-13B-pt, Redwood-Safety-13B)? We'll prioritize candidates that hit the 200ms p95 goal under our typical arrival rate.
- Procurement: I'll cc procurement on any SOC/contract artifacts you send.

We'll upload the prompt samples to the Drive link you provided and ping you when ready. If you can share the preliminary per-model p95 bench within 24 hours after we upload, that would be ideal.

Best,
Maya
